newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA sees rates, currencies helping H2.
newsitem.headline: PSA sees rates, currencies helping H2.

text.p: French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen said European currency shifts and French interest rates, if they remain at current levels, will have a positive impact on the group's second-half results.

"French interest rates, if they remain at current levels, and the pursuit of a certain re-equilibrium, still insufficient, among European currencies should have a positive impact on second-half results," it said.
The group earlier reported a drop in first-half net attributable profit to 602 million francs from 1.22 billion a year earlier.

It said its 1996 first-half results were pressured by weak growth in the market, intensified competitive pressures, particularly in its home market, and the franc's strength relative to other European currencies such as the lira.
"In this context, PSA Peugeot Citroen sought the best balance between unit margins and volumes," it said.

"If the number of vehicles sold rose only around one percent and if currency levels again had a negative impact of 0.3 percent, turnover showed a strong 2.7 percent improvement of the product mix," it said, citing the success of its new Peugeot and Citroen light commercial vehicles and its Peugeot 406 saloon.
It said its European market share at the end of August was close to year-earlier levels, and it continued to push for productivity gains.
"Despite an environment marked by ever more competitive pressures, the group possesses the best resources for the future," it said.
